title: Toscana's Metano Flips Below the National Average as GPL Keeps Climbing
dek: A look at how Tuscany's four tracked fuels have moved since July — and where the region now diverges from the rest of Italy.
executive_summary: Today's snapshot in Toscana: self-service Benzina sits at €1.9699/L, down from €2.0117 as of the Nov. 8 reading and about half a cent below the €1.9753 national average. Gasolio is at €2.2380/L, essentially identical to the €2.2381 national figure. GPL has climbed to €0.8323/L, now running above the €0.8280 national average, and Metano is flat at €2.0990/L, just under the €2.1138 national mark. Of Toscana's 1,654 registered stations, 1,492 reported a price today — a 90.2% reporting rate in line with Italy's 90.4%.

Zoom out to the weekly data since the week of July 20 and the real story is a split between two fuels moving in opposite directions relative to the rest of the country. GPL is up 11.1% in Toscana versus 9.1% nationally — the region is outpacing Italy on this fuel with no pullback yet. Metano, despite being by far the biggest mover of all four fuels (+36.0% in Toscana, +40.9% nationally since July), has flipped from trading at a 2.9% premium over the national average in July to roughly a 0.7% discount today — a crossover worth watching as it plays out.

fuel_sections.heading: Benzina Slips Back Below Two Euros, Erasing Its September Spike
paragraphs: Self-service Benzina in Toscana is €1.9699/L today (served €2.1446), down from €2.0117 as of the Nov. 8 reading — a drop of about 2.1% in six days. That puts the region roughly half a cent, or 0.3%, below the €1.9753 national self-service average.

Zooming out, Benzina has essentially round-tripped since late July: Toscana opened the tracked period at €1.9727 (week of July 20), climbed to a tracked high of €2.1658 the week of Sept. 21 — a run-up of 9.8% — and has since slid all the way back to today's €1.9699, net unchanged from 17 weeks ago. The national average traced almost the identical arc (+9.7% to the same September peak, then -8.8% back down), so Toscana isn't diverging from the rest of the country on this fuel.

fuel_sections.heading: Diesel Cools Off After Its Autumn Surge, Tracking the National Retreat
paragraphs: Gasolio self-service in Toscana is €2.2380/L today, down slightly (-0.5%) from €2.2483 on Nov. 8, and now sits essentially on top of the €2.2381 national average — a gap of roughly a tenth of a cent.

Over the full tracked window, Gasolio is up 2.9% in Toscana since the week of July 20 (€2.1737 to today's €2.2380), but that net figure masks a sharper round trip: the region peaked at €2.3833 the week of Sept. 21 (+9.6% from July) before giving back most of the gain. Nationally the pattern matches — up 9.2% to the same September peak, now up only 2.9% net — so Toscana's diesel market is moving in lockstep with the rest of Italy.

fuel_sections.heading: GPL Is the Quiet Outperformer, Rising Faster in Toscana Than Nationwide
paragraphs: GPL self-service in Toscana jumped to €0.8323/L today from €0.8153 on Nov. 8 — up 2.1% in six days — and is now running above the €0.8280 national average, a premium of roughly half a cent.

This is the fuel where Toscana is genuinely diverging from the rest of the country. Since the week of July 20, GPL is up 11.1% in Toscana (from €0.7493) versus 9.1% nationally (from €0.7592), and unlike Benzina and Gasolio there has been no pullback — GPL has climbed in nearly every week on record, with the steepest single jump landing in the most recent week alone. If that pace holds, Toscana's GPL premium over the national average is only going to widen.

fuel_sections.heading: Metano's Rally Is the Biggest of All Four Fuels — and Toscana Just Fell Behind the Pack
paragraphs: Metano self-service in Toscana is effectively flat today at €2.0990/L versus €2.1002 on Nov. 8, and now sits about 0.7% below the €2.1138 national average.

Metano has moved more than any other fuel this year: up 36.0% in Toscana and 40.9% nationally since the week of July 20. But the more interesting number is the crossover — back in July, Toscana's Metano traded at a 2.9% premium over the national average (€1.5437 vs €1.4999); today it sits at a 0.7% discount. Toscana's methane prices simply haven't kept pace with the national run-up, flipping the region from more expensive than average to cheaper than average in under four months.

network_section.heading: 9 in 10 Toscana Stations Are Reporting — Right in Line With the Rest of Italy
paragraphs: Of Toscana's 1,654 registered stations, 1,492 reported a price today (90.2%), almost unchanged from the 1,493-of-1,654 (90.3%) that reported on Nov. 8. Nationally, 21,669 of 23,961 registered stations reported (90.4%) — so Toscana's reporting rate is tracking the national norm within a fraction of a point.

A reporting rate holding steady near 90% both regionally and nationally suggests the gap isn't data drop-out specific to Toscana — it more likely reflects a small, fairly constant slice of registered stations (temporary closures, outages, or stations that simply don't submit same-day prices) across the whole country.

methodology_section.heading: How This Report Gets Made: No Spreadsheet, No Human in the Loop
paragraphs: Every part of this report — pulling the day's price and station data, computing the weekly regional and national averages, selecting today's spotlight region on a fixed rotation through Italy's 20 regions, and writing the analysis above — runs automatically, once a day, with no manual step in between.

That's a deliberate contrast with how this kind of tracking is usually done: a manually-maintained spreadsheet that someone has to open, paste new numbers into, and recalculate by hand every single day. This pipeline was built with Claude Code and simply runs itself.
